name: Simulation Ready Vehicle Mesh Assets
goal: Identify and characterize publicly accessible, citable vehicle 3D geometry assets suitable for physics simulation of a sedan, midsize SUV, and light pickup truck, with worldwide coverage and no restriction to peer-reviewed literature. Prioritize engineering or research-grade provenance: physically measured, reverse-engineered, scanned, teardown-derived, LiDAR-captured, or finite-element vehicle geometry with documented real dimensions, mass, curb weight, or other physical data. Also investigate whether the 2010 Toyota Yaris, 2007 Chevrolet Silverado, or 2020 Nissan Rogue CCSA/NCAC models have ever been converted by a third party from LS-DYNA keyword format to OBJ, PLY, glTF, USD, or another general-purpose mesh format and publicly shared.
summary:
The strongest simulation-ready assets are the CCSA/NCAC reverse-engineered LS-DYNA finite-element vehicles: 2010 TOYOTA YARIS sedan, 2012 TOYOTA CAMRY midsize sedan, and 2007 CHEVROLET SILVERADO quad-cab light pickup, each tied to teardown/scanning, measured or calibrated mass/inertial and subsystem behavior, and full-scale NHTSA NCAP validation [Mar13, Mar13b, Mar14b, Moh10].

ASSET HIERARCHY AND USABILITY.
- L2, physically measured, structural/dynamic models: NCAC/CCSA models are the only directly documented class set here that supports defensible physical-result claims. THE CAMRY WAS DISMANTLED PART-BY-PART; parts were catalogued, scanned, thickness-measured and material-classified, WITH MODEL MASS AND INERTIA CHECKED AGAINST THE PRODUCTION VEHICLE [Mar14b]. YARIS AND SILVERADO INCLUDE FUNCTIONING SUSPENSION/STEERING and extended impact validation [Opi12, Mar13b]. They are solver-native FE assets, rather than general-purpose surface meshes.
- L1/L2, historical measured FE assets: scanned/digitized Ford Taurus [Var93], Lumina/Intrepid with component/full-vehicle mass and inertia matching [Gup99], and Crown Victoria teardown/digitization plus material and component tests [Kir99].
- L0/L1, external aerodynamic/perception geometry: DrivAerML supplies CC-BY-SA, open-format meshes, but they are 500 parameter-morphed generic DrivAer variants, not measured production vehicles [Ash24]. DrivAerNet++ remains design/aerodynamics-oriented [Elr24b]. 3DRealCar supplies smartphone scans with real-world dimensions, useful exterior geometry but no documented mass/structural mechanics [Du24b].

NO CITABLE, PUBLICLY REDISTRIBUTABLE OBJ/PLY/GLTF/USD CONVERSION of the specified Yaris, Silverado, or Rogue models is verified in this result set. CarCrashNet is an explicitly unreviewed 2026 preprint describing open crash-simulation data derived partly from Yaris/Silverado models, not evidence of a general-purpose mesh conversion [Elr26].
